title: Graydon Exception to Public Bidding - Amendment No. 3, Services Agreement - Frontline Technologies Group LLC - Technology Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 2526-0156 - Authorizing Use Of Graydon Exception To Public Bidding For Amendment No. 3 To Master Services Agreement With Frontline Technologies Group DBA Frontline Education, [Wayne, PA], and Amendment No. 3, by and between District and Frontline Education, for the latter to provide licensing, hosting, upgrades and support for the absence and substitute management, employee evaluation, and professional growth platforms for the period July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2029 for an amount not to exceed $1,019,870.42 [consisting of a) $323,511.63 for 2026-27, b) $339,687.21 for 2027-28, and c) $356,671.58 for 2028-29], increasing the Agreement not to exceed amount from $3,175,729.23 to $4,195,599.65. All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.]
headline: Adds $1.02M to keep Frontline's staff absence, evaluation and training software through 2029
summary: The district is adding $1,019,870.42 to its contract with Frontline Education for software that manages staff absences and substitutes, employee evaluations and professional growth, with hosting, upgrades and support from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2029. The total contract limit rises from $3,175,729.23 to $4,195,599.65. The district is skipping public bidding under a legal exception to public bidding (called the Graydon exception).
pulled_from_consent: Adopted in its own vote on June 29 (5–1), instead of with the rest of the consent report.
outcome_action: Adopted

title: Services Agreement - East Bay Agency for Children - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement by and between the District and East Bay Agency for Children, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide coordination of the daily operations and ongoing development of the Central Family Resource Center at Lakeview;  provide oversight of the Health Insurance Enrollment Initiative, conducts family trainings, purchase of outreach materials, oversight of the Family Health Advocate Program, and provision of outreach and linkage of services to families through a Family Resource Specialist, as needed, via the Community Schools and Student Services Department, for the period July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, in an amount not to exceed $67,562.00.
headline: Pays East Bay Agency for Children up to $67,562 to run Lakeview's family resource center

It would also oversee a health insurance enrollment effort, family trainings and a Family Health Advocate program, and connect families to services. The agreement runs July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027 and is capped at $67,562.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2026-2029 and A Data Sharing Agreement – Essential School Solutions, LLC (ESS) – Special Education Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement (SA) and a Data Sharing Agreement (DSA), each, by and between the District and Essential School Solutions, LLC, for the latter to provide one full-time mental health clinician and one full-time mental/behavioral health technician to provide federally and state mandated IEP services to the students enrolled in the Counseling enriched self-contained program at Oakland Academy of Knowledge and Fruitvale Elementary School, for a total of 2 each, to provide the services, as described in Exhibit A of the Agreement, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, for the period of July 13, 2026 through June 30, 2029, in an amount not to exceed $3,134,100.00 30, 2028 and under the DSA, defining the terms and conditions of the District’s transmission of or sharing of data with Essential School Solutions, LLC, and the protection by Essential School Solutions, LLC, of such data, for the same term as the SA, each, via the Special Education Department.
headline: Pays Essential School Solutions up to $3,134,100 for mental health staff at two schools through 2029
summary: Essential School Solutions, LLC would provide one full-time mental health clinician and one full-time mental and behavioral health technician for each of two special education counseling classes, at Oakland Academy of Knowledge and Fruitvale Elementary. The staff deliver services required under students' Individualized Education Programs (IEPs). The agreement runs July 13, 2026 through June 30, 2029 and is capped at $3,134,100. A separate data-sharing agreement covers how student data is shared and protected.
schools: Oakland Academy of Knowledge; Fruitvale Elementary School
source_issue: The text gives a term ending June 30, 2029, but the garbled phrase after the amount ('30, 2028') suggests a different end date, leaving the term unclear.
pulled_from_consent: Adopted in its own vote on June 29 (5–1), instead of with the rest of the consent report.
outcome_action: Adopted

title: Services Agreement – The Crucible – The Young Adult Program
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement by and between the District and The Crucible, Oakland, CA, for the latter to host a class codesigned by Crucible and Young Adult Program staff that teaches trade skills relating to bike repair and shop organization, as described in Clause 1 of the Agreement, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, via the Young Adult Program, for the period of August 1, 2026 through June 30, 2028, in an amount not to exceed $30,000.00.
funding_source: Title I - Basic Grant Low Income Funding
headline: Ratifies up to $30,000 for The Crucible to host a bike repair trade-skills class for the Young Adult Program
summary: The Crucible would host a class, designed together with Young Adult Program staff, that teaches trade skills such as bike repair and shop organization. The agreement runs August 1, 2026 through June 30, 2028 and is capped at $30,000, paid from Title I funds.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: No Cost Services Agreement and Data Sharing Agreement - MISSSEY, Inc. (Motivating, Inspiring, Supporting, and Serving Sexually Exploited Youth) - High School Linked Learning Office
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a No Cost Services Agreement (SA) and a Data Sharing Agreement (DSA), both, by and between the District and MISSSEY Inc. (Motivating, Inspiring, Supporting, and Serving Sexually Exploited Youth), Oakland, CA, for the latter, under the SA, to provide prevention and support programs for youth attending OUSD schools, with this initiative centering youth voices, strengthen protective factors, and providing culturally responsive education and supportive services for young people who may be vulnerable to sexual exploitation, trafficking, and other forms of sexual violence and programs and/or services as further described in Exhibit A of the SA,  for the term commencing August 3, 2026 through July 30, 2029, and under the DSA, defining the terms and conditions of the District’s transmission of or sharing of pupil data with MISSSEY, Inc. and the protection by MISSSEY, Inc., of such data pursuant to the terms and conditions stated in the DSA, for the same term as specified in the SA; each Agreement, at no cost to the District.
headline: Ratifies a no-cost MISSSEY agreement for prevention and support programs for vulnerable youth
summary: MISSSEY, Inc. would offer prevention and support programs for students who may be vulnerable to sexual exploitation, trafficking and other sexual violence, centered on youth voices. A second agreement sets rules for sharing student data with MISSSEY and protecting it. Both run August 3, 2026 through July 30, 2029 at no cost to the district.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment No. 1, Services Agreement and Data Use Agreement - Care Solace, Inc - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, Services Agreement (SA) and a Data Use Agreement (DUA), each, by and between the District and Care Solace, Inc., Los Angeles, CA, for the latter, under the SA, to continue to provide a) Software-As-A-Service ("SaaS") platform through which Oakland Unified School District ("OUSD") and its authorized users may access Student Services Information Management Services, Care Coordination Services, and b) Care Companion Services; c) "All-in-One EMR" Billing Services, each as defined in Exhibit A of the SA, in the additional amount of $86,000.00, increasing the not-to-exceed amount for the SA from $86,000.00 to $172,000.00 and extending the term of the SA from July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026 to June 30, 2027 and the DUA, defining the terms and conditions of the District’s transmission of or sharing of pupil data with Care Solace, Inc., and the protection by Care Solace, Inc., of such data, for the same term as the Amended, SA, each, via the Community Schools and Student Services Department
funding_source: Alameda Alliance for Health; Alameda County Office of Education
headline: Adds $86,000 and one year to Care Solace's student care-coordination platform, now up to $172,000
summary: This amendment lets Care Solace, Inc. keep providing its online platform for student services information and care coordination, plus care companion and billing services. It adds $86,000, raising the cap from $86,000 to $172,000, and extends the term from June 30, 2026 to June 30, 2027. A data use agreement covering how student data is shared and protected is extended to match.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: [No Cost] Services Agreement 2025-2026 - The Regents of the University of California, on behalf Cal Performances at its Berkeley Campus - United for Success Academy
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a [No Cost] Services Agreement by and between the District and the Regents of the University of California, on behalf Cal Performances at its Berkeley Campus, for the latter to provide to the District at its United for Success Academy during the 2025-2026 School Year Arts integration lessons in all 6th grade History classrooms, more specifically described in Exhibit A of the Agreement, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, for the period of March 1, 2026 through April 30, 2026, at no cost to the District.
headline: Approves no-cost arts lessons from Cal Performances for United for Success Academy 6th graders
summary: Cal Performances at UC Berkeley would teach arts integration lessons in all 6th grade History classrooms at United for Success Academy during the 2025-2026 school year. The service period is March 1 through April 30, 2026, which falls before this June 24, 2026 meeting. It is at no cost to the district.
vendor_name: The Regents of the University of California, on behalf of Cal Performances
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Grant Award - Eat.Learn.Play. Foundation - Academics and Instruction Department

title: Amendment No. 1, College and Career Access Pathways (CCAP) Partnership Agreement - Peralta Community College District and District - High School Linked Learning Office
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1,  College and Career Access Pathways (CCAP) Partnership Agreement by and between the District and the Peralta Community College District (PCCD), Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide the College and Career Access Pathway (CCAP), complying with the requirements outlined under AB 288, memorializing the collaboration for the CCAP Program, and setting forth the mutual rights and responsibilities and the terms of the relationship of the Parties and the Courses, for District students enrolled in the CCAP at PCCD, extending the term of the Agreement from July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2026 to June 30, 2027. All other terms and condition of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
funding_source: College and Career Access Pathways (CCAP), Measure H, Strong Workforce Grant, and Golden State Pathways Program funding.
headline: Extends Peralta college-course partnership for OUSD students one year to June 2027, no added cost
summary: This amendment extends the College and Career Access Pathways (CCAP) agreement with Peralta Community College District, which lets OUSD students take college courses, by one year to June 30, 2027. The agreement follows state law AB 288. No money is added and all other terms stay the same.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: No Cost Services Agreement (SA) and a Data Sharing Agreement (DSA) - 3Ls The Academy - Chief Academic Officer
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a No Cost Services Agreement (SA) and a Data Sharing Agreement (DSA), both, by and between the District and the 3Ls The Academy, Oakland, CA, for the latter, under the SA, to provide  (1) family literacy workshops, offered on evenings or weekends, (2) student tutoring, delivered by trained and fingerprinted tutors; and (3) principal leadership coaching, focused on building site capacity for literacy improvement, each, at Acorn Woodland, Fred T Korematsu Discovery Academy, La Escuelita Elementary, Oakland Academy of Knowledge, Laurel Elementary, and Horace Mann Elementary Schools, for the term commencing July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2030, and under the DSA defining the terms and conditions of the District’s transmission of or sharing of pupil data with 3Ls The Academy and the protection by 3Ls The Academy of such data, pursuant to the terms and conditions stated in the DSA, for the same term as specified in the SA, each Agreement, at no cost to the District.
headline: Ratifies no-cost literacy workshops, tutoring and coaching from 3Ls The Academy at six schools through 2030
summary: 3Ls The Academy would offer family literacy workshops on evenings or weekends, student tutoring by trained and fingerprinted tutors, and principal leadership coaching on building literacy at six elementary schools. A second agreement sets rules for sharing student data and protecting it. Both run July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2030 at no cost to the district.
schools: Acorn Woodland; Fred T Korematsu Discovery Academy; La Escuelita Elementary; Oakland Academy of Knowledge; Laurel Elementary; Horace Mann Elementary
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment No. 1, No-Cost Services Agreement - Oakland Promise – High School Linked Learning Office
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1,  No-Cost Services Agreement by and between the District and the Oakland Promise, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide four programs: 1) Brilliant Baby for infants and their parents; 2) Kindergarten to College for elementary students in Kinder through 5th grade; 3) College Access supporting middle school and high school students throughout the city; and 4) College Completion for scholarships and persistence services to public school graduates while in career technical education programs, two or four-year college, to District students, as described in Exhibits A & B of Agreement, at named schools, incorporated herein as though fully set forth, via the Linked Learning Office, extending the term of the Agreement from August 1, 2024, through October 31, 2026 to October 31, 2029, at no cost to the District.
headline: Extends Oakland Promise's no-cost college-access programs from October 2026 to October 2029
summary: This amendment extends Oakland Promise's no-cost agreement by three years, to October 31, 2029. The programs are Brilliant Baby, Kindergarten to College, College Access and College Completion, which serve children from infancy through college. No money is involved.
source_issue: Appears to duplicate R.-110 (same Oakland Promise extension).
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2025-2026 - Marzano Resources - MetWest High School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2025-2026 by and between the District and Marzano Resources, Bloomington, IN, for the latter to conduct four guided work sessions where teachers will be introduced to the concept of proficiency scales as the basis for PLC (Professional Learning Community) conversations and actions; dive into the "why" of mastery based learning and teaching approach, identify priority standards, and build proficiency scales that will support the work they will be doing for the remainder of the semester, with  training divided into specific focuses based on the learning focused questions of the PLC process; materials provided, for the period of February 2, 2026 through May 29, 2026, via MetWest High School, in an amount not to exceed $7,917.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $7,917 for Marzano Resources to train MetWest High School teachers on proficiency scales
summary: Marzano Resources would lead four guided work sessions for MetWest High School teachers on proficiency scales, which are used to plan Professional Learning Community (PLC) discussions about mastery-based learning, and on choosing priority standards. Materials are included. The work ran February 2 through May 29, 2026, before this Board vote, and is capped at $7,917.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Alameda County Office of Education Services Agreement - Immigrant and Newcomer Support - English Language Learner and Multilingual Achievement (ELLMA)
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of an Alameda County Office of Education Service Agreement by and between the Alameda County Office of Education (ACOE), Hayward, CA, and the District, for latter to provide training, capacity-building, and continuous coaching to staff of the Alameda County Office of Education (ACOE) and school districts in Alameda County serving immigrant and newcomer students and families, more specifically … outlined in more detail in the Exhibit A, which is attached and incorporated herein by this reference, for the term of July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, in an amount not to exceed $300,000.00.
headline: Provides immigrant and newcomer support training to county staff under a deal worth up to $300,000
summary: The district would provide training, capacity-building and ongoing coaching to Alameda County Office of Education staff and to other Alameda County school districts on serving immigrant and newcomer students and families. The agreement runs July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027 with an amount not to exceed $300,000. The funding source is listed as the county office, so this appears to be money coming in to the district.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

It is also an oversight and operating agreement. The cumulative amount is not to exceed $287,300.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

group: Measures N and H Commission - David Kakishiba, Chairperson - June 9, 2026
title: Measures N and H Commission - Oakland Unity High School - Measures N and H Memorandum of Understanding - School Year 2026-2027
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education, upon recommendation by the Measures N and H Commission, of the Measures N and H Memorandum of Understanding by and between District and Oakland Unity High School for Fiscal Year 2026-2027, to ensure that revenues from the 2014 College and Career Readiness for All Act (“Measure N”) and revenues from the 2022 College and Career Readiness for All Act (“Measure H”, together with Measure N, ”Measures”) are spent in strict accordance with the Measures and is also an oversight and operational agreement that outlines and defines the Parties’ respective operational and reporting responsibilities for the Measures, in a cumulative amount not to exceed $249,900.00.
